output.question: Independently look up three unrelated facts and report all three: (1) the boiling point of water at sea level in degrees Celsius, (2) the speed of light in vacuum in metres per second, and (3) the height of Mount Everest above sea level in metres.
output.findings:
The boiling point of water at standard atmospheric pressure (sea level) is commonly cited as 100 °C. More precise scientific measurements place it at approximately 99.97 °C.

The speed of light in a vacuum is defined as an exact constant in the International System of Units (SI). Its value is precisely 299,792,458 metres per second.

The height of Mount Everest above sea level is 8,849 metres.
